_comment: Single source of truth for every tunable constant in the crowd renderer and the asset
pipeline, per CONSTITUTION.md section 1.2 and TESTING_AND_BALANCE.md section 5.
Nothing here may be duplicated as a literal inside code. Changing a value here is a
benchmarked change and belongs in CHANGELOG.md under Built.

troop._comment: One troop type through the whole of ASSETS.md section 4. Troop code is generic per CONSTITUTION.md section 6.1: no real weapon, faction or nationality.
troop.name: Rifleman
troop._height_comment: 1 unit = 1 metre, ASSETS.md step 4. Chosen as the measured height of a 1950s-60s infantryman in webbing; a crowd LOD is judged against it, not against the source file's arbitrary units.

skeleton._comment: The ONE shared skeleton, ASSETS.md section 4.1. Listed in build_troop.py as SHARED_SKELETON and written to assets/processed/shared_skeleton.json so gear, other bodies and future animations rig to the same thing. 25 joints: 65 minus 40 finger bones. Each joint costs a texel column and a matrix per animated vertex.
skeleton._weapon_joint_comment: A held prop is bound rigidly to one joint with weight 1.0. Under GPU skinning the same baked matrix that moves the hand moves the rifle, so no per-instance CPU work is needed.

clips._comment: Chosen from the 43 in Universal Animation Library 2. The library has no plain walk or run cycle, so the carry walk is the closest thing to a marching gait. A walk cycle and an idle is all a crowd needs; everything else in the library is for close-up combat.

budgets._comment: ASSETS.md section 5.2. Troop is 'body + gear + head' so the body mesh and the weapon are budgeted separately against one 12k total.

textures._comment: ASSETS.md section 5.1, character_body row. Downscaled, not just declared.
textures._grade_comment: ASSETS.md step 6, the shared colour grade. ART_AND_AUDIO.md section 2 style is an OPEN decision (stylized low-poly vs gritty semi-realistic vs period filter), so this is a documented NEUTRAL placeholder grade, not a locked look. It exists to prove the step runs and to make the screenshot check meaningful. Replace it when Phase 2 locks the direction.

grade._comment: Step 6 unify. Applied to the base colour map so every asset in the set sits in the same light. Neutral placeholder pending the ART_AND_AUDIO.md section 2 decision.

weapon._comment: Real-world dimensions, not the source file's units. A 1950s-60s infantry rifle is 900 mm from muzzle to butt, which is what sets the scale factor.
weapon._placement_comment: Z-up OBJ to Y-up glTF, then positioned in the right hand. The offset is in the skeleton's local space, hand_r at the origin, +X forward, +Y up.
weapon._aim_comment: Direction the barrel points, in mesh space. +Z is the direction the body faces, so this is 'forward and slightly up'. Y is nudged so the muzzle clears the hand.
weapon._offset_comment: Metres from the hand joint's bind position, in mesh axes. Pushed forward along +Z so the grip sits in the palm rather than behind it.

impostor._comment: ASSETS.md section 4.3 far tier, and ART_AND_AUDIO.md section 7 requires the silhouette to read at distance. Angles across the horizontal circle, frames down the animation clip.

lod._comment: Tuned by measurement, not assumption (ASSETS.md 4.3, SPEC.md 5.1). Produced by tools/lod-tune.mjs from the grid below. Distances are horizontal distance from the camera to the unit, in metres, in an empty scene with no terrain occlusion, so a real battle scene with cover will need these re-measured. This grid was produced on a machine BELOW the mid-range spec, so real mid-range hardware should hold a larger close tier than the one chosen here. Re-run this tool on the target hardware before shipping.

evidence.measuredOn: MacBookPro12,1, Intel Core i5-5257U @ 2.70GHz, Intel Iris Graphics 6100, 8 GB RAM, macOS 12.7.6
evidence.repeatIsolation: one browser per sample, closed before the next; two live WebGL pages split the GPU and halve the frame rate
evidence.statistic: median and minimum over the repeats, both reported
evidence.selectionRule: Largest closeMaxM whose MEDIAN clears the target with at least 10% headroom AND whose WORST single sample still clears the bare target, with at least 25 units in the close tier. Judging on the median alone once certified a 22 m close tier on a tight 34.3-34.5 spread, and a later run of the same build then dipped to 27.8 fps, below target. The worst-sample clause exists because of that.
evidence.vsyncNote: Frame rate is VSYNC-capped at 60. A reading of 60.0 means the renderer sustained the display refresh rate, not that 60.0 was measured as a throughput figure.
evidence.chosenReason: closeMaxM=20 m is the largest close tier satisfying the rule: median 44.4 fps (1.48x the target), worst sample 41.4 fps, 118 units in the close tier at 1000 units.
